title: Ask Garden: seedlings and opportunity log
body:
Purpose and framing
- Quick synthesis for product/eng of small, testable asks surfaced in field calls (mar 15–mar 28). Not a full roadmap input — this is a seedbed of low-effort experiments + a handful of higher-impact asks that could be scoped as spikes.
- Use gardening metaphor: seedlings = early, small asks we can plant as quick probes; beds = clusters of related asks to grow together; compost = customer pain context to reuse when designing fixes.

Topline signals (one-liners)
- Several mid-market customers want token-level cost windows tied to model routing decisions (e.g., when requests fall back to a cheaper model, show the delta).
- Multiple infra/platform teams report hard-to-predict latency spikes under blended workloads despite autoscaling being enabled — appears correlated with cold KV-cache misses and cross-model kernel swaps.
- A few customers on Private deployments request a simplified canary toggle (UI + API) that can pin traffic % to a private model variant without juggling rollout YAMLs.
- Request for a small "cost estimate" preview in Console when changing batching/quantization settings for a model.

Seedlings (quick probes, 1–2 week effort)
1) "Delta tag" on responses (hosted API)
   - What: A response header or minimal metadata flag showing which model variant and a small estimated token-cost-delta compared to the default model (e.g., model: rw-medium-1, delta_est_cents: -0.002).
   - Why: Customers want to audit when automated routing uses cheaper variants. Low product friction and can be surfaced as read-only in Console/Logs.
   - Risks/unknowns: Accurate delta needs stable pricing and token accounting; for streaming responses we can emit at request completion.
   - Linked artifacts: CS-1127, quick spike with billing team.

2) "KV-warm hint" for predictable latency
   - What: An optional request flag (warm_kv=true) that will route to nodes with warmed caches (best-effort). If capacity not present, returns hint header (kv_warm_ok: false).
   - Why: Engineering teams running synchronous user-facing flows prefer predictable p95 even at slightly higher cost.
   - Complexity: Routing and capacity awareness work in runtime; conservative rollout to Dedicated first.

3) Inline cost preview in Console for tuning knobs
   - What: When user changes batching size or toggles a quantization profile in Console, show projected cost impact (per-1k tokens) and expected latency change band.
   - Why: Reduces churn in support and helps self-serve optimization.

Beds (related requests to bundle into an experiment, 2–6 week)
A) "Routing transparency pack"
   - Pieces: Delta tag (seedling 1), Console routing visual (timeline of which model served when), and per-route fallback logs grouped by cause (capacity vs region).
   - Outcome hypothesis: If customers can see why routing changed they will be less likely to file incidents and can tune policies themselves.
   - Signals to track: reduction in routing-related CS tickets, increased self-serve config changes.

B) "Private deploy canary toggle + API"
   - Pieces: Simple Console slider (0–100%) for Private model variant, matching API endpoint for infra automation. Add audit log + rollout snapshot for compliance.
   - Why: Customers doing regulated rollouts want minimal friction and an auditable trail.
   - Dependencies: Console team, private control-plane gating.

Compost (customer pain context — reuse when PRD-ing)
- Example A: Fintech customer reported an incident where a rapid promotional traffic spike pushed many requests into fallback model, increasing cost by ~18% without ops noticing. They want a notification threshold when aggregated cost delta > X/day.
- Example B: Marketplace platform running many short chat completions sees latency p95 spikes when different model architectures share the same GPU pool — suspected kernel-switching overhead. They are open to pinning models per pool at a small premium.

Unresolved questions / discussion points
- Accuracy tolerance for the delta_est_cents value: are we okay with ballpark estimates (±20%) for early probe? Billing team needs to sign off.
- Placement of canary slider audit logs for Private: should they live in customer-managed S3 or in Redwood's audit store? (compliance teams will prefer customer-managed).
- KV-warm hint semantics: is "best-effort" sufficient or do customers want a blocking/wait option that holds request until warmed (risking client timeouts)?

Evidence snippets (actual customer quotes)
- "We had a week where our inference bill spiked and we still don't know why. If the API said which model variant answered each request, that's half the battle." — SRE lead, mid-market search company.
- "I can tweak quantization settings but I don't know if I'm making it worse — a quick cost/latency preview would save us from opening tickets." — Platform engineer, edtech.
- "Private rollouts are messy with our change control. A slider that spits out an audit snapshot would be ideal." — Security PM, healthcare startup.

Suggested next steps (practical)
1) Run a mini-spike for Delta Tag (CS + Billing + Serve Runtime): determine cost accuracy and header format. Owner: Leah M. Estimated: 1 week to prototype, 2 weeks to internal dogfood.
2) Triage ENG-4598 with runtime lead to instrument quick KV-warm hint prototype (Dedicated only for initial test). Owner: Marcus C. Estimated: 2 weeks.
3) Design brief for Console cost-preview micro UI (product + console eng). Owner: Priya N. Include a simple mock and a small A/B plan for self-serve users. Estimated: 1 week for mock, 3–4 weeks for implementation depending on backend hooks.

Quick wins for CS team to mitigate current friction
- Add a canned response template for routing-related cost questions that explains delta tag upcoming probe and how to pull per-request model metadata from raw logs.
- Offer a 30-minute "cost audit" for customers flagged for >15% week-over-week cost deltas.

Notes to self / internal housekeeping
- Capture results of spike in Confluence page (linked above).
- Schedule brown-bag with runtime team to go over kernel-switch observations (aim for Apr 9).

Appendix: minimal header spec proposal (for spike)
- x-redwood-model-id: rw-medium-1
- x-redwood-routing-reason: capacity-fallback | policy-route | explicit-pin
- x-redwood-estimated-delta-cents-per-1k: -0.002
- x-redwood-kv-warm-ok: true|false

End (this doc lives as a living log — update with signal outcomes and ticket links).
